title: connection-stabilizer-and-rollback-interlock-for-ephemeral-tenant-surge
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Recent incident (SUP-1123) showed cascading connection churn from ephemeral tenant surges that caused repeated KV cache invalidations and aggressive rollback attempts. The oscillation pushed regional SLOs over threshold and amplified latency spikes when many rollbacks replayed simultaneously. Motivation: reduce cascade by stabilizing short-lived connections and coordinate rollback operations with circuit state so rollbacks do not trigger mass reopen cycles. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce Connection Stabilizer component in serving/conn_manager: reserves ephemeral slots for short-lived sessions, emits soft backpressure to clients instead of hard rejections during transient surges. 2) Add Rollback Interlock in runtime/rollback: a lightweight coordinator that sequences rollback operations and rate-limits rollback-triggered state transitions while honoring the existing circuit-breaker state to avoid reopen flaps. 3) Add feature flag (deploy/featureflags.yaml) and canary rollout path (helm changes) so this behavior is opt-in for staged verification. 4) Telemetry: new metrics and tracing spans (console/telemetry/metrics.yaml + traces) to observe reservation hit-rate, stabilizer backpressure, interlock queue length, and rollback pacing. 5) Hotfix: fix race in connection reaper discovered during integration; improved locking reduces stray NPE observed under load. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for reservation logic and interlock pacing - [x] Integration tests under synthetic tenant surge - [x] Load bench (10k concurrent ephemeral sessions) in perf-canary - [x] Canary rollout in us-west-2 (24h) then progressive enable across regions - [x] Docs and console surface updates (docs/running/connection-stabilizer.md) Testing & validation: ran full unit test suite and targeted integration scenario that previously reproduced the incident; bench results show 6-9% increase in 95p latency for background steady traffic at the canary region but 35-50% reduction in rollback storms and 22% reduction in KV invalidation rate during surge windows. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; enable in staging, run 24h smoke + perf; canary enable in us-west-2 with 2% traffic for 2h, then 10% for 6h, then 100% for 24h if metrics stable; if any SLO regression >1% or error spike >0.5%, rollback to flag-off. Migration notes: no user-visible API change. Console will show new metrics under Routing > Connection Stabilizer. Related work: follows up on ENG-2199 (tenant-surge-mitigation prototypes) and aligns with existing circuit state improvements in ENG-2210. Rollback method: merged via squash after reviewers approved.

Asha Patel: Added per-tenant reservation counters and a fairness allocator; documented behavior in the description and metrics YAML.
Mei Chen: The rollback pacing default looks conservative. Suggest a lower initial window for canary to reduce latency impact.
Asha Patel: Adjusted default pacing to be aggressive only when circuit is closed; added feature flag to tune pacing per deployment.
Ravi Singh: Verified integration run in staging (logs & traces attached). Approving pending CI pass.
Mei Chen: Approved after seeing bench numbers showing rollback storm reduction and acceptable 95p latency degradation in the canary region.
release_notes: Connection Stabilizer and Rollback Interlock: reduces rollback cascades during ephemeral tenant surges; introduces a feature flag and telemetry; staged canary rollout recommended; tradeoff: small 95p latency increase under steady load in canary observed; configurable via feature flags and pacing settings.
